criteria.criterion: A new note under docs/design/ names throughput review 20261111-055051-tjym and cites THROUGHPUT.md figures (2984.3 of 2990.6 median minutes in landing and rebuild) as evidence.
criteria.evidence: The note's 'Source:' line and section 1 name review 20261111-055051-tjym and give 2984.3 of 2990.6, labelled measured. The snapshot status prints 'median per landed job over the last 20 measured: 2990.6 min (... landing and rebuild 2984.3)', and the other five stages add up to 28.5, as the note says.

criteria.criterion: The note explains the mechanism: on verifier pass, fetch host main and build the job's single landing commit on it with Git::merge_tree (base = the job's recorded base). It says why this removes the carried-over unlanded commits that the single long-lived landing branch causes. A reader can check the cause-to-fix link in the text.
criteria.evidence: Section 2 lists the steps: fetch_remote_branch, then merge_tree(base = dispatched_from, ours = main tip, theirs = landing commit), then commit_tree, then push_branch. Section 3 pairs each cause with its fix, and says how to check the result in landings/ (one file per job commit). Grep confirmed merge_tree (lib.rs:673), commit_tree (612), push_branch (432), fetch_remote_branch (406) and dispatched_from (land.rs:105).

criteria.criterion: The note has an 'Existing code:' section naming the existing paths it reuses or extends (crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs, crates/athena-core/src/land.rs, crates/athena-core/src/gh/landing.rs, docs/design/direct-main-landing.md, docs/design/per-job-main-landing.md). It says how it differs from those earlier designs and why they did not remove the wait.
criteria.evidence: Section 4 is headed 'Existing code:' and names all five paths. Every function it names exists (land.rs: plan, resync_tip, pr_commits, classify_commit, resync_onto_merge, refuse_detached; gh/landing.rs: land_pr, publish, plan_rebase, rebase_job_branch, close_carried_prs). The note says plainly that it adds no new mechanism, and that the earlier notes are still 'proposed' and unbuilt, so the long-lived branch remains. Its figures from the earlier notes (2203.6/2252.0 and the 5.0 prediction in direct-main-landing.md, 60 of 215 and 4.6 in per-job-main-landing.md) match those notes.

criteria.criterion: The note lists alternatives considered and rejected, conflict handling (merge_tree conflict, host main moving during landing), and rollback or migration from the local branch.
criteria.evidence: Section 5 (alternatives), section 8 (migration and rollback) and the merge_tree-conflict case in section 7 are present and sound. The handling for host main moving is wrong. Section 7 says 'The push is refused as not a fast-forward of the commit's parent' and, for two jobs, 'the second push is refused'. But section 2 pushes to the job's own new branch with Git::push_branch, which lib.rs:430-431 describes as a plain push that 'Git refuses when the branch exists and commit does not descend from it'. A new per-job branch is never refused because main moved. The race really happens when the host merges the pull request (gh/client.rs MergeMethod), and the note does not cover that point.

criteria.criterion: The note states the predicted saving of 5.0 minutes per landed job (from a median of 2990.6) and how the next throughput review measures it: the same THROUGHPUT.md landing-and-rebuild median, compared with the prediction, for jobs landed after the change. It also says a change implementing the design must cite review 20261111-055051-tjym in its request text.
criteria.evidence: Section 6 states the prediction of 5.0 minutes per landed job from 2990.6, labelled a prediction. The measurement uses the same landing-and-rebuild median over jobs landed after the change, compared with 2984.3 and with the 5.0 prediction. Section 9 states the citation requirement word for word.

findings.summary: The handling for host main moving and for two jobs landing at once relies on a push refusal that cannot happen.
findings.evidence: Section 2 step 5 pushes each commit as the job's own new pull request branch with Git::push_branch. lib.rs:430-436: a plain push that git refuses only when the branch already exists and the commit does not descend from it. A move of host main never makes that push fail, so neither the refetch-and-retry nor the 'second push is refused' happens. The real race is at the host merge (gh/client.rs MergeMethod, the host merge endpoint), where the host can squash a pull request built on an old tip without any check. A better design would detect the move at merge time, for example by checking with is_ancestor that the pull request's parent is still the main tip before merging, or by having the host require an up-to-date branch, and then rebuilding with merge_tree from a fresh fetch.
findings.location: docs/design/direct-main-merge-tree-landing.md section 7 ('Host main moves while landing', 'Two jobs land at once')

findings.summary: The 5.0-minute prediction does not fit the note's own figures or its measurement method.
findings.evidence: Section 3 says the saving is 'the real-wait part only', but quotes the real wait from verifier to first record as about 4.6 minutes, so a 5.0-minute saving would exceed the whole wait. Section 6 then measures the headline median against 2984.3, which the note expects to fall by thousands of minutes. The difference from 5.0 will therefore be very large whatever the real saving is. The note should say which figure is scored against 5.0, for example the first-record stage.

findings.summary: The roadmap item is numbered '3b' and placed between items 3 and 4.

summary: The candidate adds docs/design/direct-main-merge-tree-landing.md, a CHANGELOG entry and a roadmap item. Nothing outside docs and CHANGELOG changes. Most of the note is accurate. I ran `status --snapshot` on the evidence snapshot and its figures match: 2990.6 minutes in total, 2984.3 in landing and rebuild, and the other five stages add up to 28.5. Every function the note names exists in the code, and the figures it quotes from earlier design notes match those notes. The note gives the 5.0-minute prediction, says how the next review measures it, and says an implementing change must cite review 20261111-055051-tjym. The verdict is fail because section 7 handles host main moving during landing in a way the code cannot support. It says the job's push is refused as not a fast-forward when main moves, and that the second of two jobs landing at once is refused at push. But section 2 pushes each job to a new branch of its own with `Git::push_branch`, a plain push that git refuses only when that branch already exists. A move of main never makes that push fail. The race really happens when the host merges the pull request (Athena calls the host's merge endpoint with a MergeMethod). Someone implementing this would believe the race is handled when it is not. That makes criterion 4 unmet and is a major soundness finding. One smaller tension: the note predicts 5.0 minutes saved and calls that the real-wait part only, but quotes the real wait as about 4.6 minutes, and the measurement step compares the headline median, which the note itself expects to fall by thousands of minutes.
